requirements.requirement: Serve a package repository from local storage on node1
requirements.summary: Executor built /srv/localrepo containing the downloaded sl_3.03-17build1_i386.deb and a dpkg-scanpackages-generated Packages/Packages.gz index, then served it with python3 -m http.server bound to the node's IP on port 8080. A curl request to http://$NODE_IP:8080/Packages.gz directly returned HTTP 200 with the correct 529-byte index, confirming the repository was actually served from local storage.

requirements.requirement: Usual remote repositories are made unreachable during the demonstration
requirements.summary: iptables OUTPUT REJECT rules were added for tcp/80 and tcp/443 and verified in the ruleset; a subsequent curl to archive.ubuntu.com directly timed out (connection timed out after 5001ms), giving a directly observed unreachable state before installation was attempted.

requirements.requirement: Install a package from the local repository while remote repositories are unreachable
requirements.summary: With remotes still blocked by iptables, sources.list was rewritten to point only at the local repo, apt-get update succeeded fetching solely from the local server, and apt-get install -y sl fetched and installed the package entirely from http://$NODE_IP:8080. Post-install checks (dpkg -s, `which sl`, binary present at /usr/games/sl) confirm a real, working install, not just a reported success.

overall_summary: All three material outcomes of the task — serving a local repo from local storage, making remote repos unreachable, and installing a package from the local repo under that condition — are directly and coherently demonstrated with before/after evidence, not just asserted. The environment was fully restored afterward (firewall, apt sources, remote reachability re-confirmed). The independent node-restart evidence protocol is also complete and well-formed: a pre-restart boot_id/health baseline (6ab98831...), a backgrounded reboot with an acknowledgement returned before disconnect, a transient connection-refused state, a new boot_id (7a161f2f...) confirming a real restart, and full post-restart recovery of the sl package, restored apt sources, clean iptables, and remote connectivity. This matches the fixed before-prepare/after-executor boot-identity snapshots exactly, giving strong cross-check confidence. Hygiene is good but not perfect: a failed/timed-out http.server start command led to a slightly disorganized process-kill sequence (fully resolved), and some low-risk residue (local repo directory, sources backup directory, dpkg-dev/build-essential) was left on the node rather than cleaned up.
limitations: The failed cmd-c4b7b65b3b6447fe command's actual side effects (background python3 http.server process) had to be inferred from the subsequent ps aux/ss output rather than from the failed command's own output, since it errored with a proxy timeout rather than returning normally.
No evidence was captured of dpkg-dev/build-essential removal or /srv/localrepo/backup directory cleanup, so their final residual footprint is confirmed present rather than confirmed absent.

operational_hygiene.summary: Core test artifacts were cleanly restored: iptables rules removed, original sources.list/sources.list.d restored, remote apt-get update re-confirmed working, and the local HTTP server process stopped (cmd-774a3e07b02d4701, cmd-14d864ac2c6d4d69, cmd-f277f83ffbcf4b0d). However, several minor issues reduce the score: (1) cmd-c4b7b65b3b6447fe (starting the http.server via nohup+curl) errored out with a 120s proxy read timeout, but had actually started the server in the background; this required an extra diagnostic (cmd-55d9ce0d9b234d9c) and the first kill attempt (cmd-7cb7d57409f248bd, killing the wrapper bash pid 17620) did not stop the actual python3 process (pid 17622), which was still listening after the later cmd-14d864ac2c6d4d69 cleanup attempt and only stopped by the final cmd-f277f83ffbcf4b0d — fully resolved by end of task but reflects a messy kill sequence. (2) The local repo artifacts (/srv/localrepo) and the sources-list backup directory (/home/antrieb/sources-backup, including a failed permission-denied attempt at /root/sources-backup in cmd-5f8b53697e644731) were left in place rather than cleaned up; these are low-risk residue directly tied to demonstrating the task, not unrelated experimentation. (3) dpkg-dev/build-essential were installed as a prerequisite for dpkg-scanpackages and left installed, which is a reasonable, low-risk, task-justified mutation. No destructive, broad, or security-weakening residue was found; all network/firewall/apt-source state was fully restored and reboot-verified.
